ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a common-emitter amplifier circuit. The input signal ui is connected to the transistor base through the coupling capacitor C1, and the base is also connected to +VCC through RB; the collector is connected to +VCC through RC, and the output terminal is connected to the load RL through the coupling capacitor C2; the emitter is connected to the common ground line. The output uo is marked across the two ends of RL. Reasoning: According to AC small-signal equivalent treatment, C1 and C2 are regarded as short circuits, and +VCC is taken as AC ground. Therefore, in the collector AC path, RC and RL are in parallel. Given β=50, rbe=1.2 kΩ, RC=6 kΩ, RL=3 kΩ. First find the equivalent collector load: RC||RL=(6 kΩ×3 kΩ)/(6 kΩ+3 kΩ)=2 kΩ. The common-emitter voltage gain formula is Au=-β(RC||RL)/rbe, so Au=-50×2 kΩ/1.2 kΩ=-83.33, approximately -83.3.

method.method_draft: From the image, replace C1 and C2 by shorts and +VCC by AC ground, so RL is in parallel with RC at the collector. Read beta = 50, rbe = 1.2 kOhm, RC = 6 kOhm, RL = 3 kOhm from the text. Compute RC||RL = 6k||3k = 2 kOhm. Then use Au = -beta(RC||RL)/rbe = -50*2k/1.2k = -83.3.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the figure as a common-emitter transistor amplifier: emitter is tied to the bottom reference node, input ui is coupled to the base through C1, RB connects base to +VCC, RC connects collector to +VCC, and output uo is taken through coupling capacitor C2 across load RL from collector side to ground.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the numerical values RC = 6 kOhm, RL = 3 kOhm, beta/current amplification factor = 50, and rbe = 1.2 kOhm; the requested quantity is the voltage gain Au.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: At midband, coupling capacitors C1 and C2 are AC shorts and the DC supply VCC is AC ground. For a common-emitter stage with emitter grounded, the collector/load resistance is RC || RL, base current ib = ui/rbe, collector current ic = beta*ib, and the output voltage is inverted: uo = -ic(RC||RL). Thus Au = uo/ui = -beta(RC||RL)/rbe.

method.method_draft: From the image, perform a DC check with C1 and C2 open: base is biased through RB from VCC and emitter is grounded. Use VCC = 24 V, UBE = 0.7 V, RB = 800 kOhm to get IB = (24-0.7)/800k, then IC = 50 IB; the resulting collector voltage with RC = 6 kOhm is not saturated, so the common-emitter gain formula applies. For the signal circuit, short C1 and C2 and take +VCC as AC ground, giving collector load RC||RL = 2 kOhm. Use gm = beta/rbe = 50/1.2k S and Au = -gm(RC||RL) = -(50/1.2k)*2k = -83.3.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The figure is a common-emitter transistor amplifier. The emitter is connected to the bottom reference/ground node. The base is biased from the +VCC top node through RB, and the input ui is coupled to the base through capacitor C1. The collector is connected to +VCC through RC, and the output is taken from the collector through coupling capacitor C2 to the load RL, whose lower end is grounded.

Reasoning: For the DC check, capacitors C1 and C2 are open, so only RB biases the base from VCC and the emitter is grounded. The base current is IB = (VCC - UBE) / RB = (24 - 0.7) / 800 kΩ = 29.125 μA. With β = 50, IC = βIB = 1.456 mA. The DC drop on RC is IC RC = 1.456 mA × 6 kΩ = 8.74 V, so the collector voltage is about 24 - 8.74 = 15.26 V; the transistor is not saturated, so the small-signal common-emitter gain formula applies. For AC, C1 and C2 are short circuits and +VCC is AC ground, so the collector load is RC || RL = 6 kΩ || 3 kΩ = 2 kΩ. Using gm = β / rbe = 50 / 1.2 kΩ, the voltage gain is Au = -gm(RC || RL) = -(50 / 1.2 kΩ) × 2 kΩ = -83.3.
